app.analytics.page.title: Data analytics
app.analytics.page.intro: Findings from the evaluations of the three tools: collective gaps, relationships between dimensions, segments, effectiveness of measures and scenario simulation.
app.analytics.overview.title: General overview
app.analytics.overview.question: How is the set of organisations doing today in each tool, where are the weaknesses concentrated and how has it evolved over time?
app.analytics.overview.compute: For each organisation its **latest evaluation** of each tool is taken. The global score is the weighted mean of the sections (section weight) and each section the weighted mean of its KPI (KPI weight), on a 1–10 scale. Mean, median and standard deviation (σ) are computed over those scores.
app.analytics.overview.read: **≤ 5** is the critical zone (red), **5–7** the middle zone (amber) and **≥ 7** the high zone (green). The **median** is more robust than the mean when there are extreme organisations; a high **σ** indicates a heterogeneous group (some doing very well, others very poorly).
app.analytics.overview.lookFor: Tools with a low mean or many organisations in the critical zone; sections with the lowest mean (these are the collective gaps); whether the monthly trend rises after action plans start.
app.analytics.overview.findingBestWorst: The tool with the best average performance is **{{best}}** ({{bestAvg}}) and the weakest **{{worst}}** ({{worstAvg}}), with {{worstCritical}} organisations in the critical zone.
app.analytics.overview.findingDispersion: The group is most heterogeneous in **{{tool}}** (σ = {{sd}}): support should be segmented rather than applying a single strategy.
app.analytics.overview.findingSections: In **{{tool}}** the weakest section is **{{weak}}** ({{weakAvg}}, critical in {{weakRate}} of organisations) and the strongest **{{strong}}** ({{strongAvg}}).
app.analytics.overview.findingCoverage: There are **{{critical}}** critical KPI in total and **{{measures}}** registered measures ({{done}} completed): coverage of measures over critical KPI is {{coverage}} — the rest are detected gaps that still have no plan.
app.analytics.overview.statCoverageHint: Critical KPI that already have a measure
app.analytics.overview.toolSummary: {{orgs}} organisations · {{critical}} critical KPI · {{done}}/{{total}} measures completed (average progress {{progress}}%)
app.analytics.overview.histDescription: How many organisations fall into each global score range (latest evaluation).
app.analytics.overview.histRead: Each bar is a 2-point range. If the mass sits to the **left** (0–4), most of the group is in a critical situation; if it sits to the **right** (8–10), the group is mature. Two "humps" indicate two distinct subgroups (see the Typologies tab).
app.analytics.overview.histNoteMedianAbo: The median exceeds the mean: a few very low organisations drag the mean down.
app.analytics.overview.histNoteMeanAbove: The mean exceeds the median: a few very high organisations lift it.
app.analytics.overview.histNoteEqual: Mean and median coincide: symmetric distribution.
app.analytics.overview.radarDescription: Average of each section (dimension / area / principle) across the three tools. S1…S6 is the section number in each tool.
app.analytics.overview.radarRead: The **farther from the centre**, the better the section. A polygon "dented" toward the centre on one axis marks the weak section of the group; a small, regular polygon indicates widespread weakness. Compare shapes across tools to see whether weaknesses are cross-cutting.
app.analytics.overview.trendDescription: Average global score of the evaluations completed each month.
app.analytics.overview.trendRead: Each point is the average of the evaluations **completed that month**. A line rising after measures were registered suggests the plans are taking effect (confirm it in the Effectiveness tab). Months without a point had no completed evaluations.
app.analytics.overview.detailDescription: Mean, range and percentage of organisations in the critical zone for each section of each tool.
app.analytics.gaps.title: Systemic gaps
app.analytics.gaps.question: Which KPI of the {{tool}} tool fail in many organisations at once and should therefore be tackled collectively (joint training, shared technical assistance)?
app.analytics.gaps.compute: For each KPI we count in how many organisations it is **critical** (score ≤ 5) in their latest evaluation. The **systemic priority** combines three things: critical rate × KPI weight × (6 − mean). A KPI that fails in many organisations, weighs heavily in its section and has a low mean rises to the top.
app.analytics.gaps.read: **Critical in**: fraction and % of organisations where the KPI is red. **Mean**: average KPI score in the group. **Coverage**: of the critical organisations, how many already registered a measure. **Priority**: the higher it is, the more worthwhile it is to intervene on that KPI for the whole group.
app.analytics.gaps.lookFor: KPI with high priority and low coverage (nobody is addressing them); sections that concentrate many critical KPI; organisations that appear red in almost every section of the heat map (they need comprehensive support, not a one-off measure).
app.analytics.gaps.findingTop: The most systemic gap is **{{kpi}}**: critical in **{{rate}}** of the {{orgs}} organisations (mean {{avg}}); only {{coverage}} of them have a measure. It is the best candidate for a collective intervention.
app.analytics.gaps.findingUncovered: Frequent gaps that **nobody is addressing** (coverage < 50%): {{codes}}. They should be planned before others with less impact.
app.analytics.gaps.findingSection: The section concentrating the most critical KPI is **{{section}}** ({{count}} accumulated critical cases): a cross-cutting programme on that section would benefit several organisations at once.
app.analytics.gaps.findingWeakestOrg: The organisation with the lowest global score is **{{org}}** ({{score}}); the heat map shows whether its weakness is widespread (red row) or concentrated in one section.
app.analytics.gaps.topDescription: The ten KPI with the highest expected return if addressed collectively.
app.analytics.gaps.topRead: Bar length is the priority (critical rate × weight × gap). Hover to see in what percentage of organisations it is critical. Two KPI with the same critical frequency are ordered by weight and mean: the heavier and worse one goes first.
app.analytics.gaps.topNote: Scale: KPI #1 is worth {{value}}. A value of 0 means no organisation in the group has that KPI in red.
app.analytics.gaps.heatDescription: Score of each section in the latest evaluation of each organisation, ordered from lowest to highest global score.
app.analytics.gaps.heatRead: Each **row** is an organisation and each **column** a section. Deep red = score ≤ 5, amber = 5–7, green = ≥ 7. A mostly red **column** is a collective gap; a mostly red **row** is an organisation that needs comprehensive support.
app.analytics.gaps.rankingDescription: Filter by section, search a KPI or show only uncovered gaps. Click a card to see the affected organisations and a suggested reading.
app.analytics.ranking.readingBase: This KPI is critical in **{{critical}}** of {{evaluated}} evaluated organisations ({{rate}}), with mean {{avg}} and weight {{weight}} within its section. {{tail}}
app.analytics.ranking.readingNone: No organisation has registered a measure to close it yet: it is a candidate for a collective intervention (joint training, shared technical assistance).
app.analytics.ranking.readingFew: Only {{n}} organisation(s) have a measure; the good practice should be extended to the rest.
app.analytics.ranking.readingMost: Most already have a measure under way; progress needs follow-up.
app.analytics.corr.title: Correlations and drivers
app.analytics.corr.question: Which sections explain most of each tool's global score? Are organisations that are strong in one tool also strong in the others? Do the organisation's size or age matter?
app.analytics.corr.compute: The **Pearson correlation coefficient (r)** between −1 and 1 is used over the organisations that have both variables. For the **drivers**, each section score is correlated with its tool's global score; for the **cross-tool** view, each section of one tool with each section of another; for the **factors**, the number of members and age (years since start) with the global score, adding a simple linear regression.
app.analytics.corr.read: **r near 1**: when one rises, the other rises (direct relationship). **r near −1**: inverse relationship. **|r| ≥ 0.7** strong, **0.4–0.7** moderate, **0.2–0.4** weak, less: no relationship. Only pairs with at least {{minSample}} organisations are shown. Correlation does **not** imply causation: it shows where to look.
app.analytics.corr.lookFor: Driver #1 of each tool is the section with the most leverage; strong pairs across tools reveal cross-cutting capabilities (improving one pulls the other); profile factors with moderate or strong r suggest segmenting support by size or maturity.
app.analytics.corr.findingGlobal: The global score of **{{toolA}}** and that of **{{toolB}}** have a **{{strength}}** correlation (r = {{r}}, n = {{n}}): organisations strong in one tend to be strong in the other, so organisational strengthening acts as a cross-cutting enabler.
app.analytics.corr.findingDriver: In **{{tool}}** the section that best explains the global score is **{{section}}** (r = {{r}}): improving it is the most efficient lever to raise the tool's result.
app.analytics.corr.findingPair: The most related pair of sections across tools is **{{a}}** ↔ **{{b}}** (r = {{r}}): an intervention on the first will probably also impact the second.
app.analytics.corr.findingFactor: The most influential profile factor is **{{factor}}** in {{tool}} (r = {{r}}, {{strength}}{{slope}}): {{group}} organisations start at a disadvantage and need more intensive support.
app.analytics.corr.driversTitle: Drivers: which section explains the global score
app.analytics.corr.driversDescription: Correlation of each section with its tool's global score. The bar measures |r|; the number is r.
app.analytics.corr.driversNote: ★ = main driver. Note: a heavily weighted section always correlates highly with the global score by construction; the relevant finding is when a **low-weight** section correlates strongly, because it points to a capability that "goes with" the rest.
app.analytics.corr.scatterDescription: r = {{r}} · {{strength}} relationship · {{n}} organisations with both evaluations
app.analytics.corr.scatterRead: Each point is an organisation: X axis its score in {{toolA}}, Y axis in {{toolB}}. Points aligned along a rising diagonal = strong direct relationship. Points **far from the diagonal** are "unbalanced" organisations: strong in one tool and weak in the other — they deserve individual analysis.
app.analytics.corr.matrixTitle: Correlation matrix between sections of different tools
app.analytics.corr.matrixDescription: Green = positive correlation, blue = negative; more intense = stronger. Hover to see full names and n.
app.analytics.corr.matrixNote: How to read it: look for the most intense cells. A strong green cell between, say, ORG-5 (Clients / Markets) and CAP-1 (Capabilities) says that organisations with good market access also have better compliance capabilities: they probably share a common cause (professionalised management). Blue (negative) cells are rare and deserve review.
app.analytics.corr.factorsDescription: Relationship between the organisation's characteristics and its global score in each tool.
app.analytics.corr.factorsNote: The regression slope indicates how many global score points change per additional member or per year of age; R² is the share of variation that factor explains (0–1). If age weighs more than size, institutional maturity matters more than scale.
app.analytics.eff.title: Effectiveness of measures
app.analytics.eff.question: Do action-plan measures really improve the KPI? How much more does a critical KPI improve when a measure is assigned and completed, compared to one where nothing was done?
app.analytics.eff.compute: Organisations with **at least two completed evaluations** of the same tool are taken. For each KPI, **Δ = score in the latest − score in the first** is computed. KPI that were critical in the first are split into three groups by the registered measure: **completed**, **in progress** or **none**. Non-critical KPI serve as the control group. Attributable effect = Δ(with completed measure) − Δ(without measure).
app.analytics.eff.read: Each bar is the group's average improvement (points from 1 to 10). If "with completed measure" is clearly higher than "without measure", the measures work. The control group should stay near 0: if it also rises, the improvement could be due to another cause (e.g. a change of evaluator). "% improved" is the fraction of KPI in the group that rose at least 1 point.
app.analytics.eff.lookFor: Attributable effect above 1 point; measures in progress with an intermediate Δ (consistent: half done, half the effect); positive correlation between % of completed measures and the organisation's global improvement. If "without measure" improves as much as "with measure", review the quality of the measures or of the evaluation process.
app.analytics.eff.noHistory: There are no organisations with two completed evaluations of the same tool yet; the analysis will activate with the first re-evaluation.
app.analytics.eff.findingBest: Measures **do work**: in {{tool}}, critical KPI with a completed measure improved **{{done}}** points on average ({{improved}} improved) versus {{none}} for those without a measure: attributable effect ≈ **{{effect}}** points.
app.analytics.eff.findingOther: In **{{tool}}** the attributable effect is {{effect}} points ({{orgs}} re-evaluated organisations; Δ with completed measure {{done}}, in progress {{open}}, without measure {{none}}).
app.analytics.eff.findingControl: The control group of {{tool}} (non-critical KPI) moved {{delta}} points: {{tail}}
app.analytics.eff.controlStable: stable, which reinforces that the improvement comes from the measures and not from evaluator bias.
app.analytics.eff.controlMoved: an appreciable change, so part of the improvement could be due to external factors.
app.analytics.eff.findingDoneRatio: In {{tool}}, the share of completed measures per organisation relates in a **{{strength}}** way to its global improvement (r = {{r}}): {{tail}}
app.analytics.eff.doneRatioStrong: closing measures is what moves the score, not just planning them.
app.analytics.eff.doneRatioWeak: completing measures helps, but other factors also weigh on the global improvement.
app.analytics.eff.chartDescription: {{orgs}} re-evaluated organisations · average global improvement {{delta}} points
app.analytics.eff.chartRead: Compare the **"with completed measure"** bar with **"without measure"**: the difference is the effect of the measures. The **control** bar (non-critical KPI) should be near zero. Red bars indicate worsening. n = number of KPI compared in the group.
app.analytics.eff.tableDescription: Global score in the first and the latest evaluation, and how many measures each organisation completed in between.
app.analytics.seg.title: Segmentation
app.analytics.seg.question: Are there performance differences between groups of organisations by {{label}}? Which group needs the most support?
app.analytics.seg.compute: Organisations are grouped by the chosen attribute ({{label}}). For each group and tool the mean global score (latest evaluation), its standard deviation and the average number of critical KPI per organisation are computed.
app.analytics.seg.read: Compare bars of the same colour across groups: the difference in points is the **gap between segments**. A high σ within a group indicates it is not homogeneous. Groups with fewer than 3 organisations are not statistically conclusive.
app.analytics.seg.lookFor: Groups consistently below in all three tools (they need a differentiated strategy); gaps above 1 point; groups where only one tool is low (a specific, not structural, problem).
app.analytics.seg.findingSpread: The largest difference between groups is in **{{tool}}**: **{{max}}** averages {{maxV}} versus {{minV}} for **{{min}}** (gap of {{diff}} points). Interventions should be differentiated by {{label}}.
app.analytics.seg.findingOther: In **{{tool}}** the gap is {{diff}} points ({{max}} {{maxV}} vs {{min}} {{minV}}).
app.analytics.seg.findingSmall: The groups {{groups}} have fewer than 3 organisations: their averages are indicative, not conclusive.
app.analytics.seg.chartDescription: One bar per tool within each group.
app.analytics.seg.chartRead: Compare bars of the **same colour** across groups. If a group has the three lowest bars, its disadvantage is structural; if only one is low, the problem is specific to that tool.
app.analytics.seg.detailDescription: Mean · standard deviation · critical KPI per organisation, for each tool.
app.analytics.clusters.strategyHIGH: Maintain and document good practices; they can act as mentor organisations for the rest.
app.analytics.clusters.strategyMEDIUM: Action plans focused on their weakest section; quarterly follow-up.
app.analytics.clusters.strategyINTERVENT: Comprehensive, intensive support: several sections red at once; prioritise with the simulator.
app.analytics.clusters.title: Organisation typologies
app.analytics.clusters.question: What "types" of organisations exist in {{tool}} according to their pattern of strengths and weaknesses, and which support strategy fits each type?
app.analytics.clusters.compute: Each organisation is represented as a vector with its score in each section (latest evaluation). The **k-means** algorithm groups organisations into **k** clusters minimising each one's distance to the centre (centroid) of its cluster. Initial centroids are chosen deterministically so the result is reproducible.
app.analytics.clusters.read: A cluster's **centroid** is its "typical organisation": the radar shows its score per section. The **label** (high / medium / requires intervention) comes from the centroid's mean. Each cluster shows its strongest (▲) and weakest (▼) section and its member organisations.
app.analytics.clusters.lookFor: Clusters with a clearly different profile (not just "better and worse" but with different weaknesses) — they justify differentiated strategies. Try k = 2, 3 and 4: if raising k produces a single-organisation cluster, k is too high for the sample size.
app.analytics.clusters.findingSummary: With k = {{k}} there are {{n}} typologies: {{list}}. The algorithm converged in {{iterations}} iterations.
app.analytics.clusters.findingCluster: The **{{label}}** cluster excels in **{{strong}}** ({{strongV}}) and falters in **{{weak}}** ({{weakV}}). Suggested strategy: {{strategy}}
app.analytics.clusters.findingSingleton: There is a cluster with a single organisation: with this sample, k = {{k}} may be too high; try k = {{suggested}}.
app.analytics.clusters.radarDescription: Typical score of each cluster in each section.
app.analytics.clusters.radarRead: Each polygon is a cluster. The farther from the centre on an axis, the better that section. Two polygons with similar shapes but different sizes are "same profile, different level"; different shapes indicate different weaknesses and therefore different strategies.
app.analytics.sim.title: What-if simulator
app.analytics.sim.question: If an organisation improves certain critical KPI up to a target score, how much would its global score rise and which KPI should be prioritised?
app.analytics.sim.compute: The score is recomputed with the tool's **same weighted mean**: each section is the weighted mean of its KPI and the global score the weighted mean of the sections. A KPI's **sensitivity** is how much the global score rises per point that KPI rises: (KPI weight ÷ sum of weights in its section) × (section weight ÷ sum of weights).
app.analytics.sim.read: Each row is a critical KPI (≤ 5) of the chosen evaluation. Move the slider to the target score and watch the gauge: **current → projected**. Presets set several KPI at once. "Global/point" is the sensitivity: for equal effort, start with the highest values.
app.analytics.sim.lookFor: How many KPI need to move to cross a threshold (e.g. leave the critical zone ≤ 5 or reach 7); whether the most sensitive KPI coincide with the systemic gaps (double return); sections that barely move even when KPI improve (low weight).
app.analytics.sim.findingLever: Biggest lever: **{{code}}** ({{name}}) — each point it rises adds **+{{gain}}** to the global score.
app.analytics.sim.findingTop5: The five critical KPI with the most effect are {{codes}}; taking them to 6 would raise the global score from {{from}} to {{to}}.
app.analytics.sim.findingCeiling: Taking **all** critical KPI to 8 would give {{score}}: that is the ceiling reachable by tackling only the critical ones; the rest of the margin lies in the middle-zone KPI.
app.analytics.sim.noCritical: This evaluation has no critical KPI.
app.analytics.sim.bySectionNote: The faint bar is the current value and the solid one the projected value. A section that barely changes even when you move its KPI has little weight in the global score.
app.applicability.title: Applicable KPI — {{name}}
app.applicability.description: Untick the sections or KPI that do not apply to this organisation (e.g. "only if it carries out forest harvesting"). They will not be required when completing evaluations nor counted in the score. Applies to new and ongoing evaluations.
app.applicability.saved: Applicable KPI updated for this organisation.
app.applicability.noTemplate: There is no active template for this tool.
app.gantt.empty: There are no measures to show in the schedule.
app.risk.countryParams.title: Risk threshold by country
app.risk.countryParams.description: The evaluated organisation's country defines the negligibility threshold: a KPI scored above the threshold is classified as a negligible risk. Without a row for the country, the template threshold (5) applies.
app.risk.countryParams.empty: No country parameters: the template threshold is used.
